# Free third-party material

Code and files from other projects that are free software, the kind Debian main takes. XeStrata may build and run
with them. Each project's folder keeps its own license text.

| Folder | Project | License | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ggml/` | [ggml / llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) | MIT (`ggml/LICENSE`) | `ggml-common.h`, an unmodified copy at the commit in `ggml/VERSION.txt` (it stays MIT): the block layouts and codebook grids of the quantized formats. `ggml-common-tq.h`, from upstream Strata's copy of Agention's llama.cpp fork (agentionai/llama.cpp 073bc9e68, MIT): the trellis formats of the Gyro files (TQ2_T, TQK6, TQK7) and their codebook, unchanged. Needed to build the engine. Update it only together with the pinned llama.cpp (the engine also links ggml-cpu from it) |
| `intel-llvm/` | [intel/llvm](https://github.com/intel/llvm) (DPC++) | Apache-2.0 with LLVM exceptions (`intel-llvm/LICENSE.TXT`) | Not the compiler itself, which `tools/intel_llvm_build.py` clones from intel/llvm at the release it pins (v7.2.0) and builds into `.tools/`: XeStrata's fixes to it, `patches/NN-<id>.patch`, which the script applies in order before building. They are under intel/llvm's license, as changes to its files; each says what it fixes. The deb and rpm packages carry the SYCL runtime of the intel/llvm built so (`libsycl`, UR's loader and adapters, `libumf`), with this license text |
| `rocm-device-libs/` | [ROCm's device libraries](https://github.com/ROCm/llvm-project/tree/f30ae3e6b680ad23dcf522e668c6d4c5c90838d0/amd/device-libs) (ocml, ockl and the others), by AMD | University of Illinois/NCSA (`rocm-device-libs/LICENSE.TXT`) | Not the libraries themselves, which `tools/intel_llvm_build.py` clones from ROCm's llvm-project at the commit it pins (ROCm 7.14.1's, on the same LLVM as the intel/llvm it builds) and builds with intel/llvm into `.tools/`, with the target features Debian's rocm-llvm package gives their build (transcribed from its `debian/rules`, Expat: see NOTICE); without them CMake takes a ROCm's device libraries the compiler reads (`cmake/StrataHip.cmake`). The AMD code links them: the engine's kernels for AMD GPUs carry parts of them, so the deb and rpm packages carry this license text |
| `oneDNN/` | [oneDNN](https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneDNN) | Apache-2.0, with the parts other projects' licenses cover (`oneDNN/LICENSE`, `oneDNN/THIRD-PARTY-PROGRAMS`) | Not oneDNN itself, which `CMakeLists.txt` fetches at the tag it pins (`v3.12`, its archive's SHA-256 checked), or takes from `STRATA_ONEDNN_SOURCE`, and builds with the engine's compiler for Intel GPUs only (its SYCL GPU runtime) beside the build. The image engine's attention on Intel GPUs (its SDPA, `src/image/qi_sdpa_onednn.cpp`); the text engine does not load it. Windows: cross-built as the engine is, without its VTune hooks (`DNNL_ENABLE_JIT_PROFILING`, `DNNL_ENABLE_ITT_TASKS`: their assembly is MASM's), and `dnnl.dll` goes into the 7z. Ubuntu's `libdnnl-sycl` is built for another SYCL runtime than intel/llvm's, so it is not used |
| `cudnn-frontend/` | [cuDNN Frontend](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend) | Apache-2.0, parts MIT (`cudnn-frontend/LICENSE.txt`) | Not the headers themselves, which `CMakeLists.txt` fetches at the tag it pins (`v1.31.0`, its archive's SHA-256 checked) in the contrib-llvm mode where cuDNN's own headers are found: the image engine's attention on NVIDIA GPUs (cuDNN's SDPA, `src/image/qi_sdpa.cpp`), Linux and Windows. cuDNN itself is NVIDIA's and not free software: the engine opens it at run time where the user installed it (`libcudnn.so.9`, `cudnn64_9.dll`), and takes its own kernel without it. Header-only, compiled into the image engine: the contrib-llvm packages and the Windows 7z carry this license text |
| `aotriton/` | [AOTriton](https://github.com/ROCm/aotriton) | MIT (`aotriton/LICENSE`); its kernels' images can carry parts of AMD's aiter (MIT, `aotriton/LICENSE.aiter`), FlyDSL's kernels (Apache-2.0, `aotriton/LICENSE.FlyDSL`) and Triton (MIT, `aotriton/LICENSE.triton`), which its build compiles them with | Not AOTriton itself, whose release `CMakeLists.txt` fetches (`0.14.2b`: the library built for the build's ROCm and the kernels' images for its AMD architectures, each archive's SHA-256 checked), or takes from `STRATA_AOTRITON_ROOT`: the image engine's attention on AMD GPUs (its flash attention, `src/image/qi_sdpa.cpp`); the text engine does not load it, and the image engine opens it, through a module of its own, on an AMD GPU only. On Windows, where AOTriton has no release, the library is built from the tag's source (its NOIMAGE mode, the images Linux's) with XeStrata's patch (`aotriton/patches/`: HIP's headers and import library given, the build machine's Python; under AOTriton's license) and the 7z carries it, its images and these texts. A ROCm it has no build for takes XeStrata's own kernel. The deb and rpm packages carry its library and images, with these license texts |
| `xz/` | [XZ Utils](https://tukaani.org/xz/) | 0BSD (`xz/COPYING.0BSD`) | Not XZ Utils itself, whose release `CMakeLists.txt` fetches (`5.8.1`, its archive's SHA-256 checked) on Windows: its liblzma, built static and linked into AOTriton's library there. The Windows 7z carries this text |
| `llama.cpp/` | [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) | MIT (its own `LICENSE`) | Not in the repository: setup fetches it at the pinned commit. ggml-cpu for the CPU experts, the image encoder's `mtmd`, and `gguf-py` for the tools. The deb and rpm packages carry `gguf-py` with llama.cpp's `LICENSE` |
| `oneMath/` | [oneMath](https://github.com/uxlfoundation/oneMath) | Apache-2.0 (`oneMath/LICENSE`) | Not oneMath itself, which `CMakeLists.txt` fetches from XeStrata's fork ([MistVVK/oneMath](https://github.com/MistVVK/oneMath), branch `xestrata`) at the tag it pins (`xestrata-10`, its archive's SHA-256 checked), or takes from `STRATA_ONEMATH_SOURCE` (a local archive or URL); in the contrib-llvm and contrib-icpx modes, and in the free mode for AMD GPUs. The fork is oneMath's commit 6ff3a43 with XeStrata's changes as commits and oneMath's `develop` merged into it (up to 1308c5e), under oneMath's license, each marking the files it changes in their headers: the cuBLAS backend's BF16 product (oneMath has none), the rocBLAS backend's 16-bit products through hipBLASLt where it has kernels for the GPU (ROCm 7.1's rocBLAS has no tuned ones for RDNA4), the int8 products with int32 output in the rocBLAS backend (through hipBLASLt likewise) and the cuBLAS backend (oneMath has them in neither), hipBLASLt's algorithms timed on a large product's first call where a program asks for it (`ONEMATH_HIPBLASLT_TUNE=1`, the image engine), the cuBLAS and rocBLAS backends' SYCL targets on their own libraries, so that one build makes both, and the rocBLAS backend without what HIP and SYCL deprecate (HIP's context API, the comparisons with `HIP_SUCCESS`, `get_access` for a host accessor), and on Windows the compile and link lines and SYCL target of the other platforms for the GNU-style clang++ driver (XeStrata's cross build from Linux), in place of clang-cl's, and the cuBLAS and rocBLAS backends, built there too, with the CUDA and ROCm headers and Windows import libraries the cross build gives. oneMath runs the dense matrix products through its oneMKL (Intel), cuBLAS (NVIDIA) and rocBLAS (AMD) backends. The deb and rpm packages carry the oneMath built so (its rocBLAS backend; the contrib-llvm ones its oneMKL and cuBLAS backends too), and the Windows 7z its oneMKL, cuBLAS and rocBLAS backends, with this license text |
| `quantscope/` | [quantscope](https://github.com/1872183316/quantscope) | MIT or Apache-2.0, at your option (`quantscope/LICENSE-MIT`, `quantscope/LICENSE-APACHE`) | `quantscope.py`, unmodified at commit bfdf205 but for a line saying where it comes from (as upstream Strata took it, #911): it reads a GGUF's headers only (a file, a folder, a URL, a ModelScope or Hugging Face repository). `tools/strata_inspect.py` and `setup.py --inspect` use it to say what a GGUF really is and whether XeStrata runs it. Without it only that check is gone |
| `stb/` | [stb](https://github.com/nothings/stb) | MIT or public domain (the Unlicense), at your option (`stb/LICENSE`, the header's own end) | `stb_image.h` v2.30, unmodified (the copy llama.cpp carries in `vendor/stb`): the image engine (`strata-image`) reads an edit's reference image with it (PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF). Needed to build the image engine |
| `outfit/` | [Outfit](https://github.com/Outfitio/Outfit-Fonts) | SIL Open Font License 1.1 (`outfit/OFL.txt`) | The web app's font (WOFF2, Latin and Latin Extended). Without it the web app uses the system font |
